description: This team will compete in the Space Game as a school!
summary:
This low-poly 3D survival and engineering game takes place stranded on a hostile planet swarming with dust storms. You take shelter in the Zorg Base or an underground aluminum mine before your suit breaches. You must mine for aluminum, find materials, and scavenge for parts to build your way home.

In order to build your rocket, you run a real pressure test that must hold 10,000 metric tons. You repair an orbital transponder by choosing the correct 48V DC bus. You salvage a LAS motor and servo motors from a wrecked rover. You assemble nozzles, casings, and a mainframe from mined scrap, and more. 

This is important because the growing space economy will need engineers fluent in systems thinking, problem solving, and resource management. The earlier this intuition forms, the stronger the future workforce pipeline. Games reach students who lack lab gear, budgets, or advanced coursework making a career in space feel reachable, not abstract.
details:
The project is a low-poly 3D survival and engineering game set on a hostile planet plagued by dust storms. Players must manage suit integrity by taking shelter in Zorg Base or an underground aluminum mine while mining aluminum, gathering raw materials, and scavenging parts to build a rocket home. Core gameplay revolves around authentic engineering tasks. First, the Structural & Propulsion Testing: Running a pressure test that must withstand 10,000 metric tons. Next, the Electrical Systems: Repairing an orbital transponder by selecting the proper 48V DC bus. Finally, the Salvage & Assembly aspect. Recovering a Launch Abort System (LAS) motor and servo motors from a wrecked rover, and fabricating nozzles, casings, and a mainframe from mined scrap.

Some key benefits this game provides are the Accessible Hands-On Learning: It gives students practical experience in systems thinking, troubleshooting, and resource management without requiring expensive lab equipment, large budgets, or advanced prerequisite coursework. Another benefit is the Risk-Free Experimentation: Players can test engineering constraints (like pressure limits and electrical bus selection) in an interactive environment where failure teaches iteration rather than causing real-world harm. Lastly, the High Engagement aspect. Wrapping technical engineering concepts inside a high-stakes survival loop keeps players motivated to solve complex mechanical and electrical problems.

This project aims to make an impact by strengthening the future aerospace and space-economy workforce pipeline by building systems-thinking and problem-solving intuition early. By making aerospace engineering approachable through gaming, it helps students—especially those in under-resourced schools—see a career in the space industry as concrete and achievable rather than abstract.

Our project show's creativity by blending Genres: Instead of treating aerospace engineering as a dry textbook quiz or sterile simulator, it integrates real engineering specs (48V DC buses, 10,000-metric-ton pressure thresholds, LAS motors) directly into a tense planetary survival narrative. Another example is the Cohesive Visual & Environmental Storytelling: Using a low-poly 3D aesthetic keeps performance lightweight while allowing dramatic environmental hazards (dust storms, wrecked rovers, underground mines) to drive the gameplay loop. The last example of this is the Scavenging-to-Engineering Loop: Turning environmental storytelling—like stripping servos from a crashed rover—into functional rocket components connects exploration directly to technical problem-solving.

Some factors our team considered were the Educational Accessibility & Hardware Performance: Choosing a low-poly 3D art style ensures the game runs smoothly on standard school or home computers without needing high-end GPUs, maximizing who can play and learn from it. Realism vs. Playability was another thing we took into account. Balancing real-world aerospace concepts (voltage buses, structural load testing, subsystem assembly) so they remain technically authentic without overwhelming players who have no prior engineering background. Lastly, Pacing & Survival Tension: Tuning environmental timers (such as dust storms and suit breaches) alongside shelter locations (Zorg Base and the aluminum mine) so players feel urgency without getting stuck in an unwinnable loop.
